citeAs: Bisk, Yonatan, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, and Yejin Choi. (2020). PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. AAAI.
creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi (Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence; Microsoft Research AI; Carnegie Mellon University; Paul G. Allen School for Computer Science and Engineering, University of Washington)
description: PIQA (Physical Interaction: Question Answering) is a benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language. Given a goal and two possible solutions, a model or human must choose the more sensible solution. The dataset is built from goal-solution pairs inspired by how-to instructions and filtered to reduce annotation artifacts.
name: PIQA
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were described as average people in the sense that tools and materials from instructables would not be unfamiliar to the average person; annotators for human evaluation had to achieve at least 90% on a qualification HIT.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Examples with low agreement were removed during validation. Human performance was calculated by majority vote, and only annotators who achieved at least 90% on the qualification HIT were chosen to participate in human evaluation on development data.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk HITs, with annotator pay reported on Turkerview.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were shown instructables for inspiration and asked to provide three components: (1) a physical goal, (2) a valid solution, and (3) a plausible but wrong 'trick' solution. They were asked to glance at an instructable and construct tasks inspired by it, often using atypical materials, and to create a permutation of their own solution that subtly made it invalid. Qualification HITs and later validation by other annotators were used, and a diff button highlighted where paired solutions differed.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly identifies reporting bias as a challenge for physical commonsense data collection, noting that people tend to produce prototypical solutions and overuse familiar kitchen or garage tools. To mitigate this, annotators were prompted with instructables to encourage more diverse and less prototypical object use, and AFLite was used to reduce annotation artifacts and spurious biases.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by prompting annotators with links to instructables.com examples from six categories and asking them to create goal-solution pairs for physical tasks. Annotators wrote a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid but plausible 'trick' solution, and additional validation HITs were run afterward.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source material was how-to instructions from instructables.com, a crowdsourced collection of instructions for building, crafting, baking, repairing, and manipulating objects using everyday materials.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that examples requiring expert-level domain knowledge were removed because they should not count as commonsense, and argues that learning about the world from language alone is limiting. It also notes that models may eventually match human performance through heavy in-domain fine-tuning, which the authors say is not the main point of the benchmark.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After collection, the dataset was filtered with AFLite, which discards instances whose feature representations are highly indicative of the target label, in order to reduce annotation artifacts and spurious biases.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was cleaned using AFLite to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples. The paper also reports tokenization with spaCy for dataset statistics and GPT BPE tokenization for length analysis.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as supporting research toward language representations that capture physical knowledge useful beyond NLP, including robotic-language applications, while also arguing that knowledge should ultimately be learned from interaction with the world and communicated with language.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking and studying physical commonsense understanding in natural language models, and for diagnosing what physical knowledge large pretrained models do or do not capture.
